newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel markets unbowed by talk of Russian influx.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel markets unbowed by talk of Russian influx.

text.p: European fuel oil markets were stable on Monday with business stilled by summer doldrums but holding firm levels, traders said.

Barges began offered around $92 a tonne and traded at $91 for July, before drifting down to $90 for the same month. August was quoted at $92/93 a tonne. Overall prices were little changed from last week.

A Scottish utility bought 20-25,000 tonnes of high sulphur fuel at several dollars over the current market range of $83/85 cif, which the buyer said reflected the forward nature of the purchase, which is due for delivery before October.

High sulphur numbers were continuing solid, despite talk of an influx of Russian material in the first half of August. Traders have talked of 120-150,000 tonnes which will come south because arb routes out of the region have shut, but others were sceptical such volumes will appear.
Low sulphur swaps have lost almost $2 since Friday, as traders sensed the arrival in mid to late August of a number of cargoes that will compete for buying interest.
